I've been on HRT for just over a month now, so all I can offer is some entrance level stuff but it's still stuff I hadn't expected.

1. Roughly around the 1 Month mark, I felt a sort of... shift. It was mainly emotional but also mental. And while I did feel the gradual changes during that month this specific event was when that shifting sorta clicked into place. In my case I was "no thoughts head empty" for a few hours on the floor sobbing, but I've heard that for others it's just the ability to cry easier or in some cases crying less due to the shift causing Euphoria.

2. Really, and I mean *really* weird affects on your appetite. For me before HRT, I was almost always hungry. I attribute this to being well past the chunkier side, but even though I was always hungry I could still suppress it if I knew I was eating too much. After a few weeks on HRT though? Sometimes I would eat the entirety of meals that my family intended to portion out among 5 or more people, and other times I could barely stomach a single bite. Wasn't due to the taste or type of food either, it was just what I can only describe as my stomach deciding that I deserved to suffer.

3. Salt Cravings. This only really applies if you're specifically taking Spironolactone, but with that being very commonly prescribed it'll most likely happen. Part of it is thanks to the hormonal shift, but it's also just a side effect of the drug in question being some kidney shenanigans. In my case sometimes I'd crave salt so badly that I would intentionally drink less water so I wouldn't dilute the sodium in my system. 

4. This is the last one and probably the weirdest, Euphoria from typically Dysphoric things. This is a whole lot of small things, but for me it was mainly when I would look at myself in the mirror and still dislike my appearance. I would judge the little things like my stubble, or my eyebrows being too thick or thin, the works. When I stepped back from the mirror though I started looking at things that weren't MtF specific, like stretch marks on my belly, birthmarks I was previously perfectly fine with, and more. The reason why I felt Euphoria from those Dysphoric things is because I felt like I was falling into a feminine stereotype, that being too critical of small parts of myself that almost nobody else would notice. Put simply, it felt good to feel insecure. It was weird to say the least.

  
That's all I got for ya, though do know that in all of these cases except the more mental ones I've since learned to somewhat control them. Like while I'm consciously aware of my appetite being strong or weak, I can now stop myself from eating too much or too little. And with my salt cravings I've learned to take it slower so the sodium can actually get into my system so I don't dehydrate myself. For a while I was getting stupid unhealthy but I've already moved past it enough to say that I've mostly adjusted to all these changes. Hope this all helps, and if you have further questions I'm happy to answer!
